protocol_summary: Countermovement jump (CMJ) - *Protocol:* hands on hips (to remove arm-swing variability) or with arm swing — pick one and never change. name: Squat jump (SJ) and CMJ - SJ difference
protocol_summary: Squat jump (SJ) - *Protocol:* squat to ~90° knee angle, hold for 3 seconds (this eliminates the stretch-shortening contribution), then jump maximally without any downward dip. 3 attempts. Recall that boxers characteristically show a very small difference (~0.9 cm reported average), some jumping higher in the SJ. A difference under 2 cm flags reactive strength as a priority. Target >4 cm.

name: Drop jump reactive strength index (RSI)
protocol_summary: Drop jump reactive strength index (RSI) - *Protocol:* step off a box (start at 20 cm, progress to 30–40 cm only when competent), land and rebound as fast and high as possible. Instruction: “minimize your time on the ground, maximize your height.” 3–5 attempts. - *Measurement:* RSI = jump height ÷ ground contact time (or flight time ÷ contact time — pick one formula and keep it). - *Introduce only when landing mechanics are competent.* This test is a plyometric exposure, not just a measurement. - *Interpretation:* trained athletes commonly 1.5–2.5+ (using height/contact-time in m/s). What matters is your trend.

name: Seated single-arm medicine ball punch throw
protocol_summary: Seated single-arm medicine ball “punch” throw — the most useful field proxy for punch force available without force-measuring equipment. - *Protocol:* seated on the floor with back against a wall (removes leg contribution) or seated on a bench (allows some trunk contribution — pick one). Ball at the shoulder in a punching position. Throw for maximum horizontal distance with a punching action. 3 attempts per arm. Measure to first contact point. - *Ball mass:* 3 kg for most, 4 kg for heavier boxers. Never change the ball mass between tests. - *Track:* lead-arm distance, rear-arm distance, and the asymmetry between them. Large asymmetry (>15–20%) is common and worth addressing. - *Validity note:* medicine ball throw distance correlates strongly with CMJ, SJ, press-up performance and sprint times, and moderately with lower-body lean mass — which is consistent with the kinetic-chain picture in Part 1 §2.2.

name: 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (VIFT)
protocol_summary: 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-15 IFT) — preferred - *Protocol:* 40 m shuttle course, 30 s of running interspersed with 15 s passive recovery, starting at 8 km·h⁻¹ and increasing 0.5 km·h⁻¹ per stage, paced by audio cues, to volitional exhaustion. - *Output:* VIFT — the velocity of the last completed stage. - *Why preferred:* it is intermittent, includes changes of direction and acceleration/deceleration, and — most usefully — it yields a directly prescribable velocity. You can then write conditioning sessions as percentages of VIFT rather than guessing. name: Repeated sprint test (percentage decrement)
protocol_summary: Repeated sprint test - *Protocol:* 6 × 35 m sprints with 10 s recovery (or 6 × 30 m with 20 s, or a bike equivalent). Record every time. - *Key metric:* percentage decrement = (total time ÷ (best time × number of sprints) − 1) × 100. A decrement under ~5% is good; over 8–10% indicates poor repeat-effort ability. - *Why decrement matters more than best time:* boxing does not require one fast sprint. It requires the twelfth burst to resemble the first.

protocol_summary: ### 7.3.1 Self-review (30 min, after every sparring session and every bout) / Pass 1 — normal speed, no notes. Overall impressions. For each: *what information was available before the action? Did I read it?
